title: Ingenuity: Utility Belt Ring Amplifier, Calculator and Charm Use in 0.5
summary: Ingenuity is a Unique Utility Belt in Path of Exile 2 0.5.4 that grants (20-30)% increased effect of Explicit Modifiers on your Left Ring and an independent (20-30)% on your Right Ring, plus Flask and Charm support. This guide covers the Ring Bonus Calculator, which ring mods are amplified, the legacy single-(40-80)% roll, the 0.2.0f charm-slot change, where it drops (King in the Mists), valuation, and community questions.
description: How Ingenuity works in Path of Exile 2 0.5.4: the Utility Belt that amplifies Left and Right Ring explicit modifiers, the Ring Bonus Calculator, the Modifier Eligibility Matrix, legacy ranges, King in the Mists drop, and trade value.
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team
imageAlt: Path of Exile 2 Ingenuity unique Utility Belt showing the (20-30)% Left and Right Ring explicit modifier amplification

sections.title: Quick answer
sections.callout: Ingenuity is a Unique Utility Belt that amplifies the explicit modifiers on your equipped rings: (20-30)% increased effect of Explicit Modifiers on the Left Ring and an independent (20-30)% on the Right Ring. It also gives 20% increased Flask Charges gained, (1-3) Charm Slots from the base, and small Charm charge modifiers. In 0.5.4 it drops from the King in the Mists pinnacle boss and cannot be made with a Chance Orb.
calloutDetail: Each ring is rolled separately, so a perfect Ingenuity can give up to 30% on the left and 30% on the right at the same time.
Only explicit modifiers on the rings are amplified - ring implicits and the belt's own mods are not.

answers.label: Use for
text: Supercharging explicit ring modifiers (life, resistances, attributes, damage) and supporting a Charm-focused defensive layer.

answers.label: Check first
text: Confirm the two ring rolls are separate and read the current 20-30 range before overpaying for a legacy 40-80 copy.

answers.label: Avoid
text: Assuming it boosts ring implicits or frees suffixes - it amplifies explicit mods only, and the belt still occupies your belt slot.

sections.title: Ring Bonus Calculator (worked examples)
sections.caption: Formula: Amplified value = base ring modifier x (1 + roll% / 100). Each ring is rolled independently.
sections.note: Opportunity cost: Ingenuity consumes your belt slot, so compare the amplified ring value against a well-rolled Rare belt (e.g. a life/resist belt). A single high-value ring mod amplified by 30% often beats a generic rare belt, but only if your rings carry strong explicit modifiers.

sections.title: Overview and current versus legacy
paragraphs: Ingenuity turns your ring slot into a multiplier. Its two headline lines each grant (20-30)% increased effect of Explicit Modifiers on one ring - the Left Ring and the Right Ring - and the two rolls are independent, so a perfect copy can hit 30% on both simultaneously. The belt also delivers 20% increased Flask Charges gained, the Utility Belt's (1-3) Charm Slots implicit, and small (-20 to 20)% Charm Charges gained / (-10 to 10)% Charm Charges used lines.

Because it multiplies explicit ring mods, Ingenuity rewards builds that invest in high-value ring modifiers (large life, resistances, attributes, or damage). A ring with a weak explicit line gains little; a ring stacked with strong explicits gains a lot.

Current versus legacy: in the current 0.5.4 range each ring is amplified by its own (20-30)% roll. Older copies rolled a single (40-80)% that applied to both rings at once - simpler but capped lower per ring and not independent. A 0.2.0f-era change also added a +(1-2) explicit Charm Slots line to some copies; the base (1-3) Charm Slots from the Utility Belt remains on all versions. Identify which generation you have before valuing it.
bullets: Current (0.5.4): separate (20-30)% Left and (20-30)% Right ring amplification.
Legacy: single (40-80)% applied to both rings together.
0.2.0f legacy: some copies also carry +(1-2) explicit Charm Slots.
Only explicit ring modifiers are amplified; implicits and the belt's own mods are not.

sections.title: Build usage
intro: Ingenuity shines wherever rings carry explicit modifiers worth multiplying. The four personas below show the main ways to use it.

Worked example recap: a Left Ring with +60 Maximum Life at a 25% Ingenuity roll becomes +75 Life (60 x 1.25); a Right Ring with +40% Elemental Damage at 28% becomes 51.2% (40 x 1.28). Both rings can be amplified at once on a perfect copy.

builds.title: Ring-stacking endgame
builds.description: Pushes two explicit-heavy rings (life, resist, attribute or damage) through Ingenuity for a large net stat gain.

builds.title: Charm-focused defence
builds.description: Leverages the base Charm Slots and charge mods for a layered defensive tech without giving up ring value.

builds.title: Flask sustain
builds.description: The 20% increased Flask Charges gained line supports a flask-heavy sustain plan.

builds.title: Hybrid attribute stacker
builds.description: Pairs with attribute-heavy rings (see the Astramentis guidance) to amplify +% attribute explicits.

sections.title: Alternatives
paragraphs: A Rare Utility Belt (or another belt base) can deliver flat life, resistances, attributes and utility suffixes that Ingenuity does not provide, at the cost of the ring multiplier. If your rings are implicit-heavy or weak on explicits, a Rare belt is often the better value.

Other Unique belts trade the ring amplifier for specialised payoffs (e.g. flask duration, armour, or charge generation). They suit narrower builds and should be considered only when ring amplification is not your priority.

Catalysts can quality the belt's own value where relevant, but they do not change the ring amplification range. Liquid Emotions and Charm tuning (see the Charms guide) are complementary systems rather than direct replacements.
bullets: Rare belt: flexible suffixes, no ring multiplier.
Other Unique belts: build-specific, weaker for ring amplification.
Catalysts / Liquid Emotions / Charms: complementary, not replacements.

sections.title: How to get Ingenuity
intro: Ingenuity drops from the King in the Mists pinnacle boss. It is a targeted Unique reward from that encounter and cannot be created with a Chance Orb, so farming the boss (or buying the roll on trade) is the only realistic path.

routes.label: King in the Mists (pinnacle boss)
body: Defeat the King in the Mists to fish for Ingenuity as a Unique drop from the fight.

routes.label: Repeat the pinnacle
body: Re-running the boss with higher difficulty or yield modifiers improves your chances of a high double roll.

routes.label: Trade (Currency Exchange / trade site)
body: Because it is boss-locked and not Chance Orb compatible, trade is often the fastest way to get a specific double roll.

routes.label: No Chance Orb path
body: Do not waste Chance Orbs on Utility Belts expecting Ingenuity - it is not in the Chance Orb unique pool.

entries.question: Does Ingenuity amplify ring implicits or only explicits?
summary: A player asked whether the belt boosts a ring's base implicit modifiers.
editorialAnalysis: Ingenuity amplifies only Explicit Modifiers on each ring. Ring implicits, the belt's own Charm Slots, and Ingenuity's own lines are excluded.
officialAnswer: Only explicit ring modifiers are amplified; implicits and the belt's own mods are not.

entries.question: Where does Ingenuity drop in 0.5?
summary: A guide summarised the drop source for the belt.
editorialAnalysis: Ingenuity is a boss-locked Unique from the King in the Mists and is not Chance Orb compatible, so the boss fight or trade are the only routes.
officialAnswer: Farm the King in the Mists pinnacle boss, or buy a specific roll on the trade site.

entries.question: How much does a 30% roll actually add to my ring?
summary: A guide walked through the belt's value with worked numbers.
editorialAnalysis: Using amplified = base x (1 + roll/100), a 30% roll adds 30% to every explicit ring modifier - e.g. +60 Life becomes +78 Life.
officialAnswer: A perfect 30% roll multiplies each explicit ring mod by 1.30; both rings can hit 30% on a perfect copy.

entries.question: Is the legacy single (40-80)% better than the current split?
summary: A video compared legacy and current generations.
editorialAnalysis: The legacy roll applied one value to both rings (max 80% on each, but not independent), while the current split gives up to 30% per ring independently - different shapes, not strictly better or worse.
officialAnswer: Compare by your two independent rolls; a perfect current copy can outperform a legacy one per ring.

problems.symptom: My ring's implicit did not increase
directAnswer: Ingenuity amplifies only explicit ring modifiers; ring implicits and the belt's own mods are excluded by design.
checks: Check that the modifier is an explicit line, then use the calculator to confirm the gain.

problems.symptom: Both rings show the same amplification
directAnswer: You likely have a legacy single (40-80)% copy, which applies one value to both rings. Current copies roll Left and Right independently.
checks: Inspect the two separate roll lines to tell legacy from current.

problems.symptom: Chance Orb on a Utility Belt did nothing
directAnswer: Ingenuity is not in the Chance Orb unique pool; it drops from the King in the Mists only.
checks: Farm the boss or buy on trade instead of using Chance Orbs.

problems.symptom: Belt feels weak on my build
directAnswer: If your rings are implicit-heavy or have weak explicits, a Rare belt is usually better. Ingenuity rewards strong explicit rings.
checks: Audit your ring explicits before committing the belt slot.
